title: Embedding model coexistence, index synchronizer, and traffic-throttle protocol
creator: Priya Nair
description: Background: As new embedding models are introduced and older models deprecated, downstream vector indexes (semantic indexes + reranker calibration) can diverge. This ticket implements a coordinated approach that lets two or more embedding model variants coexist while ensuring indexes remain query-compatible, reranker quality is preserved, and tenant traffic is shaped to avoid latency spikes. The goal is to enable safe hot-swaps and staged deprecations with minimal customer disruption and measurable rollback gates.
acceptance_criteria: Index Synchronizer service can create and keep versioned index manifests mapping model-version -> index-compatible transform spec
Shadow backfill runs for a tenant namespace without impacting foreground serving latency (p50 p99 thresholds preserved)
Traffic-throttle policy enforces per-tenant rate caps and graded ramp rules during model switchover
Reranker calibration probes detect semantic drift and trigger automated pause/rollback when quality delta > 3% on golden prompt set
Rollout playbook documented and executable by SRE/SE with step-by-step runbook and one-click rollback link
plan: Design and implement three coordinated components: (1) Index Synchronizer - a service that generates a lightweight transform spec (normalization, dimensional mapping hints, vector scaler metadata) to make new-model embeddings compatible with existing indexes where feasible. (2) Coexistence Bridge - routing layer that can serve multi-variant embeddings per-tenant and maintain mapping metadata for reranker. (3) Traffic-Throttle Protocol - policy engine integrated with rate limiter to partition traffic during ramp, with burst allowances and SLO-aware degradation. Work broken into: design doc -> proto/adapter implementation -> smoke tests -> shadow backfill -> canary -> ramp -> deprecation schedule.
telemetry_and_observability: Dashboards: embedding/index-sync (latency, backfill throughput), rerank-quality (cohort precision@k, recall@k on golden sets), tenant-latency-by-model, traffic-throttle-enforcement-rate. Alerts: rerank-quality-drop (>3% relative on critical cohort), backfill-error-rate (>1%), model-serving-p99-latency-exceed (configured SLO per tier). Add synthetic golden prompts per high-value tenant to measure semantic regression continuously.
risks: Incompatible transforms: some model pairs cannot be reconciled by a lightweight transform, requiring full index rebuilds
Backfill load could affect shared storage I/O and cause transient latency increases if not rate-limited correctly
False positives from reranker probes could unnecessarily halt rollouts if golden sets are not representative
Operational complexity: new metadata (transform specs, coexistence maps) must be resilient to schema changes
rollout_steps: 1) Design complete and review (design doc + sequence diagrams) - assign owners for each component
2) Implement Index Synchronizer prototype and unit tests + storage schema for manifests
3) Implement Coexistence Bridge routing prototype with tenant-level overrides
4) Integrate Traffic-Throttle Protocol into gateway and Redwood rate limiter (policy tests)
5) Run internal shadow backfill on non-prod tenant namespaces (monitor I/O and p99)
6) Canary: 1% traffic for 7 days with rerank-quality probes and increased telemetry sampling
7) Ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 60% -> 100% with automated checks at each step; hold conditions defined in acceptance criteria
8) Deprecation: schedule staggered index rebuild windows for tenants where transform compatibility fails
9) Post-launch: 30-day monitoring window + cost telemetry for backfill and serving overhead
implementation_notes: Prototype uses a compact JSON transform spec: {mean_shifts, norm_params, dim_map_hint}. Index Synchronizer will attempt 'lossy alignment' first (affine transform + normalization). If alignment MSE > threshold, mark tenant for full rebuild. Coexistence Bridge stores per-tenant active_model_alias and fallback_alias. Traffic-Throttle Policy supports graded rules: static-percentage, adaptive-SLO (reduce ramp if latency > threshold), tenant-priority overrides.
